captions.instagram:
What is a ballistic missile?

A ballistic missile is a rocket that pushes for a few minutes and then simply falls, along the same kind of arc as a thrown ball. Fire Newton's cannon on a curved Earth and watch an arc close into an orbit.

→ “Ballistic” means one short push, then nothing but gravity, like a thrown ball.
→ A ballistic missile is a rocket that burns for a few minutes, then coasts on a free-fall arc.
→ Newton imagined a cannon on a mountain above the air: the faster the shot, the further round it lands.
→ At about 7.9 km/s the ground curves away as fast as the ball falls: it is in orbit.
→ The push comes from a rocket built in stages: each one drops away when it is empty.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/ballisticmissileclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is a ballistic missile? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A ballistic missile is a rocket that pushes for a few minutes and then simply falls, along the same kind of arc as a thrown ball. Fire Newton's cannon on a curved Earth and watch an arc close into an orbit.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/ballisticmissileclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/ballisticmissileclear

In this video:
• One push, then free fall. Ballistic means moving under gravity alone after a single push, like a thrown ball.
• Newton's cannon. Newton imagined a cannon on a mountain above the air.
• Every arc is part of an ellipse. A free-fall path around the Earth is a piece of an ellipse with the Earth's centre at one focus, the same shape Kepler found for planets.
• Powered by rockets. The push comes from a rocket built in stages that drop away when empty.
• Names and ranges. The Arms Control Association sorts ballistic missiles into short-range (under 1,000 km), medium-range (1,000 to 3,000 km), intermediate-range (3,000 to 5,500 km) and intercontinental (over 5,500 km).
• The human cost and the treaties. By the end of 1945 the atomic bombings had killed about 140,000 people in Hiroshima and 70,000 in Nagasaki.
